title: Microsoft Azure Fundamentals - Describe cloud concepts

sections.name: Describe the benefits of using cloud services

questions.text: Which statement best describes cloud computing?

choices.text: The delivery of computing services over the internet
A single physical server located in a company's office
A software application installed locally on every laptop
A private network that cannot reach the public internet

questions.explanation: Cloud computing is the delivery of computing services - such as virtual machines, storage, databases, and networking - over the internet, so you aren't constrained by physical infrastructure.

questions.text: Under the shared responsibility model, which items are ALWAYS the customer's responsibility, regardless of the cloud service type? (Select all that apply.)

choices.text: The information and data stored in the cloud
The accounts and identities of users, services, and devices
The devices that are allowed to connect to your cloud
The physical datacenter, network, and hosts

questions.explanation: The consumer is always responsible for their data, their identities/accounts, and the devices that connect. The physical datacenter, network, and hosts are always the provider's responsibility.

questions.text: Which items are ALWAYS the cloud provider's responsibility under the shared responsibility model? (Select all that apply.)

choices.text: The data stored in the cloud

questions.explanation: The cloud provider always owns the physical datacenter, physical network, and physical hosts. Data, devices, and identities always remain the customer's responsibility.

questions.text: Which cloud service type places the MOST responsibility on the consumer?
questions.explanation: IaaS places the most responsibility on the consumer; the provider only handles physical security, power, and connectivity. SaaS places the most responsibility on the provider.

questions.text: A cloud that is built, controlled, and maintained by a third-party provider and available to anyone who wants to purchase services is a:
questions.explanation: A public cloud is built, controlled, and maintained by a third-party provider; general public availability is the key difference from a private cloud.

questions.text: A cloud environment used by a single entity, offering greater control at greater cost, is a:
questions.explanation: A private cloud is used by a single organization, providing greater control for the IT team but at greater cost and with fewer public-cloud benefits.

questions.text: Which cloud model interconnects public and private clouds, letting a private cloud 'surge' into public resources during temporary demand?
questions.explanation: A hybrid cloud uses both public and private clouds together, so a private cloud can surge into public cloud resources for temporary increased demand.

questions.text: True or False: In a multicloud scenario, an organization uses two or more public cloud providers.
questions.explanation: Multicloud means using multiple public cloud providers - for example, using different features from each, or migrating from one provider to another.

questions.text: Because you pay for cloud services only as you consume them, cloud spending is classified as which type of expense?
questions.explanation: The consumption-based model bills you as you use services, making cloud an operational expense (OpEx), unlike CapEx up-front spending on physical infrastructure.

questions.text: Which set of technologies helps you manage servers and resources across on-premises, hybrid, and multicloud environments from Azure?
questions.explanation: Azure Arc is a set of technologies that helps manage your environment whether it's public cloud on Azure, a private datacenter, hybrid, or multicloud.

questions.text: Which cloud service type is the MOST flexible and gives the consumer the maximum amount of control?
questions.explanation: IaaS is the most flexible category and provides the maximum control; you're essentially renting the hardware and manage everything above it.

questions.text: In an IaaS model, which responsibilities belong to the customer? (Select all that apply.)

choices.text: Operating system installation, configuration, and maintenance

questions.explanation: With IaaS the provider maintains the hardware, network connectivity, and physical security; you handle the OS, network configuration, and database/storage configuration.

questions.text: Which cloud service type is a 'middle ground' where the provider also maintains the operating systems, middleware, and development tools?
questions.explanation: PaaS sits between IaaS and SaaS. The provider maintains infrastructure plus OS, middleware, and dev tools, so you focus on your application.

questions.text: True or False: In a PaaS environment, the customer must handle licensing and patching for operating systems and databases.
questions.explanation: False. In PaaS you don't worry about licensing or patching for operating systems and databases - the provider maintains them. You focus on your application and data.

questions.text: Renting and using a fully developed application such as email or messaging software is an example of:
questions.explanation: SaaS is the most complete model - you use a fully developed application. Email, messaging, and financial software are common SaaS examples.

questions.text: Which cloud service type has the LOWEST operational overhead for the customer and is the easiest to get up and running?
questions.explanation: In SaaS the provider manages almost the entire stack, so the customer mainly manages data, identity/access, and device access - the lowest operational overhead and easiest to run.

questions.text: A team wants to 'lift and shift' its on-premises servers to the cloud with full control over the operating system. Which service type is the best fit?
questions.explanation: Lift-and-shift migration is a common IaaS scenario: you replicate your on-premises datacenter configuration in the cloud and move workloads while keeping full control.

questions.text: A development framework with built-in scalability plus analytics/business-intelligence tooling delivered as a service are common scenarios for which service type?
questions.explanation: PaaS scenarios include providing a development framework (with built-in scalability, high availability, and multitenancy) and analytics/BI tools delivered as a service.

questions.sectionTitle: Describe the benefits of using cloud services
questions.text: In the cloud, what does 'scalability' refer to?

choices.text: The ability to adjust resources to meet demand
The ability of a system to recover from failures
The guaranteed uptime of a service
The physical size of the datacenter

questions.explanation: Scalability is the ability to adjust resources to meet demand - adding resources at peak and reducing them when demand drops, so you don't overpay.

questions.sectionTitle: Describe the benefits of using cloud services
questions.text: Adding more CPU or RAM to an existing virtual machine is an example of:
questions.explanation: Vertical scaling increases or decreases the capabilities of a resource (for example, adding CPU or RAM to a VM). Horizontal scaling adds or removes the number of resources.

questions.sectionTitle: Describe the benefits of using cloud services
questions.text: Adding more virtual machine instances to handle a spike in demand is an example of:
questions.explanation: Horizontal scaling adds (scales out) or subtracts (scales in) the number of resources, such as adding VMs or containers to meet demand.

questions.sectionTitle: Describe the benefits of using cloud services
questions.text: Which benefit is defined as the ability of a system to recover from failures and continue to function, and is a pillar of the Azure Well-Architected Framework?
questions.explanation: Reliability is the ability of a system to recover from failures and continue to function; the cloud's decentralized, global design supports it, and it's a Well-Architected Framework pillar.

questions.sectionTitle: Describe the benefits of using cloud services
questions.text: Azure uptime guarantees that define how available a service will be are documented in:
questions.explanation: High availability focuses on maximum uptime. Azure's uptime guarantees vary by service and are defined in service-level agreements (SLAs).

questions.sectionTitle: Describe the benefits of using cloud services
questions.text: Predictability in the cloud can focus on which two areas? (Select two.)
questions.explanation: Predictability covers performance (autoscaling, load balancing, high availability) and cost (real-time tracking, forecasting, and tools like the Azure Pricing Calculator).

questions.sectionTitle: Describe the benefits of using cloud services
questions.text: 'Management in the cloud' describes how you manage your environment. Which are valid methods? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: You can manage your cloud environment through a web portal, a command-line interface, APIs, and PowerShell. Physical datacenter access is the provider's domain.

questions.sectionTitle: Describe the benefits of using cloud services
questions.text: Automatically shutting down a development environment overnight and on weekends primarily supports which cloud consideration?
questions.explanation: Turning off or deallocating resources that aren't in use - like dev environments outside business hours - reduces unnecessary consumption, supporting sustainability and cost efficiency.
